checks: The strictly isolated vertex and strict exclusions make each section a simplex with exactly the incident-edge intersections. The centroid gives t_ij=d y_j for j≠i and all of these factors lie in (0,1), so each r_j>0 and their sum is one.

The margin normalized to one at v_i gives pyramid height 1/||∇L_i||. This gives S_i u_i=d|T|q_i∇L_i with the inward sign. Expanding any constant affine combination of L_i shows its coefficients are proportional to r_i, so normalization gives θ_i=(r_i/q_i)/B.

On F_i the only absent cap is the i cap. For j≠i the edge-product area omits the factor dy_i, giving relative area q_j/(dy_i). Summing yields (1−r_i)/(Bdy_i)=1/B, including counting measure on the two interval endpoints.

Verified the derivative bracket numerator is (sum of the omitted coordinates)^2 plus the sum of their squares. Averaging unequal extreme coordinates decreases the ratio strictly when d≥2 and drops the variance by half the squared range. This forces convergence to the uniform point. In d=1 the ratio is exactly 1/2. Exact rational arithmetic replayed these facet identities and the uniform equality for d=1 through 12.

Read 05d41ace8d693538 §§1–3 and 19aecfceb071d1da §§3–5. The proof reconstructs the cofactor and averaging arguments directly, assumes the entire measured facet is isolatable, and makes no positive-width or mixed-global inference.

overlap.comparison: The accepted fact constructs an isolating field in one specified tied four-fiber triangle family and proves its positive-width payment. The reviewed result gives the conditional every-facet formula for arbitrary dimension and prescribed own section-centroid data.

readability: The balance uses own coarea and unit inward normals. The field statement conditions on its trace being constant over a whole measured facet.
